title: South Florida This Week: Halloween, FLIBS, and King Tides
igCaption:
Halloween first, boats second, flooded streets all week.

Sources: WSVN 7News, Miami New Times, NBC 6 South Florida, Sun Sentinel, South Florida Reporter

#Miami #FortLauderdale #SouthFlorida #Halloween

scenes.text: Need South Florida plans this week? Start with Halloween stops, then Fort Lauderdale gets over one thousand three hundred boats.

First, watch the water. King tides brought more flooding after a soggy weekend, and 7News cameras caught high-tide flooding Monday morning. Wind and flood advisories are in effect, so check your route before you park near low streets.

scenes.text: For Halloween plans, Miami has trick-or-treating on Halloween. Miami New Times put out a city guide, which helps if you want candy plans without turning the night into a spreadsheet.
scenes.caption: For Halloween plans, Miami has trick-or-treating on Halloween. Miami New Times put out a city guide, which helps if you want candy plans without turning the night into a spreadsheet.

scenes.text: Then Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show returns Wednesday for its 67th year. NBC 6 says more than 1,300 boats from around the world will be displayed. The show calls itself the world’s largest in-water boat show. If you're there, open NEAR and see who else is at FLIBS.

scenes.text: The boat show also has 50-plus debut vessels and over 130 superyachts. That brings buyers, crews, and marine businesses into Fort Lauderdale at the same time.

scenes.text: For Halloween road-trip people, Key West wrapped Fantasy Fest with a parade on Duval Street. The 10-day costuming celebration ended Saturday with tens of thousands of spectators, 12-foot puppets, and 125 performers in one float.

scenes.text: What are you doing first: candy, boats, or checking the tide? Between costumes, boats, and king tides, South Florida is full of people you pass without meeting, which is exactly the kind of connection NEAR helps put a name to.
